High Energy Physics - Phenomenology

arXiv:hep-ph/0105050 (hep-ph)

[Submitted on 7 May 2001]

Title: A Grand Canonical Ensemble Approach to the Thermodynamic Properties of the Nucleon in the Quark-Gluon Coupling Model

Authors: Hai Lin

View a PDF of the paper titled A Grand Canonical Ensemble Approach to the Thermodynamic Properties of the Nucleon in the Quark-Gluon Coupling Model, by Hai Lin

View PDF

Abstract: In this paper, we put forward a way to study the nucleon&#39;s thermodynamic properties such as its temperature, entropy and so on, without inputting any free parameters by human hand, even the nucleon&#39;s mass and radius. First we use the Lagrangian density of the quark gluon coupling fields to deduce the Dirac Equation of the quarks confined in the gluon fields. By boundary conditions we solve the wave functions and energy eigenvalues of the quarks, and thus get energy-momentum tensor, nucleon mass, and density of states. Then we utilize a hybrid grand canonical ensemble, to generate the temperature and chemical potentials of quarks, antiquarks of three flovars by the four conservation laws of the energy and the valence quark numbers, after which, all other thermodynamic properties are known. The only seemed free paremeter, the nucleon radius is finally determined by the grand potential minimal principle.
